title: Simultaneous Synthesis of Single-walled Carbon Nanotubes and Graphene in a Magnetically-enhanced Arc Plasma
protocol: Scale nickel powder and yttrium powder according to the molar ratio of 4.2:1 as catalyst powder.
Mix the catalyst powder with graphite powder very well.
Fill the mixed powder into a hollow graphite rod firmly.
Ensure the total molar ratio of C:Ni:Y in the anode rod is 94.8:4.2:1.
Install the cathode rod inside the cylindrical chamber.
Position the stuffed anode rod inside the cylindrical chamber with the cathode rod.
Adjust the gap distance between the cathode and anode to about 3 mm.
Place a cuboid permanent magnet inside the chamber at about 25 mm from the interelectrode axis.
Cut a 0.3 mm thickness molybdenum sheet into a 25 mm × 100 mm rectangular shape.
Remove surface contamination of the molybdenum sheet by ultrasonic dismembrator in acetone and ethanol for 30 min.
Install the molybdenum sheet attaching one side of the permanent magnet.
Turn this side of the molybdenum sheet towards the electrodes.
Measure the magnetic field in the interelectrode gap by a Gaussmeter.
Pump down the cylindrical chamber to less than 10-1 Torr vacuum.
Fill the chamber with helium (99.995%) to 500 Torr.
Connect arc electrodes to DC welding power supply.
Set up the power supply on an arc current of about 75 A.
Record real-time values of arc current, arc voltage, and chamber pressure for analysis.
Start video recording from right and front viewports simultaneously.
Run the arc for 15 seconds.
Cool down the chamber by natural convection for at least 20 minutes.
Use tweezers to tear off the deposition flake from the surface of molybdenum sheet.
Collect another sample from the black collar of cathode.
Observe the morphology of both sides of deposition flake under SEM (acceleration voltage of 30 kV).
Drop cast a suspension of methanol-dispersed SWCNT solution after sonicating for 60 minutes using ultrasonic dismembrator with 50% amplitude.
Observe the morphology of the thin film under JEOL TEM at 100 KV after volatilization of methanol solution.
Obtain electron diffraction patterns from positions of interest in sample using a CCD camera length of 50 cm associated with TEM.
Perform Raman spectroscopy on graphene flakes using a micro-Raman system based on a 200 mW Lexel 3000 Ar ion laser at 514 nm wavelength.
Cover the range of 100 cm-1 to 3100 cm-1 for Raman measurements on the surface of graphene flakes.
